scenario.title: One status. Two very different next moves.
scenario.lede: The amount is unchanged. The decision word is not.
scenario.review_question: Which source record authorizes the status shown to the customer?

impact.person: The approved $128 refund does not arrive before rent day; the customer puts groceries on a credit card.
impact.workflow: The queue closes the case as denied; the next agent restarts review without the original receipt.
impact.industry: Two support teams copy the false closure into their dashboards and train new agents on the wrong resolution.
impact.market: A renewal review uses the inflated closure rate; leadership cuts the team that still has to resolve the refunds.
impact.long_tail: The false denial becomes the template in eight later case reviews, outliving the original approval record.

cascade.text: The approved $128 refund is marked “denied”; the customer carries the shortfall into rent day.
Two case queues inherit the denial; one closes the case while the other restarts review.
Four team dashboards publish the duplicated closure as a resolved outcome.
Eight later case reviews use that false success pattern as precedent.

impact.person: The user believes the agent broadcast a transaction; the recorded run shows zero broadcasts and failed authorization.
impact.workflow: The operator marks the run complete; two reconciliation queues stop asking for the signed receipt.
impact.industry: Four incident, risk, and agent-evaluation reports repeat the broadcast despite its absence from the source record.
impact.market: Eight downstream readers treat the action as settled; a team’s response plan assumes funds moved.
impact.long_tail: The fictional execution story becomes the operational record while no transaction receipt exists.

cascade.text: A zero-broadcast dry run with failed authorization becomes “one broadcast” and “approved.”
The operator closes the run; two reconciliation and incident queues inherit the unsupported broadcast status.
Those queues copy it into four risk and evaluation reports.
Eight readers treat the broadcast as settled although no signed receipt is attached.

scenario.title: A stale-source block turns green.
scenario.lede: The same synthetic block reference receives opposite freshness and update statuses in a draft summary.
scenario.source: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — Oracle check at block 810200: freshness test failed. Price update: blocked. Source status: expired.
scenario.candidate: SYNTHETIC DRAFT — Oracle summary at block 810200: freshness test passed. Price update: approved. Source status: current.
scenario.review_question: Can the chain, block, signed update time, source identity, and protocol freshness rule substantiate the summary?

impact.person: The protocol reviewer sees “current” at block 810200 and accepts a price update whose signed source has expired.
impact.workflow: Two review queues clear the update; the stale-source alert never reaches the on-call engineer.
impact.industry: Four protocol and risk summaries carry the green freshness state into the next pricing review.
impact.market: A later incident uses those summaries as the timeline; the missing signed update obscures why the price moved.
impact.long_tail: Eight downstream decision points inherit a fresh-price narrative with no matching signed update or rule version.

cascade.text: At the same synthetic block, an expired source becomes “current” and a blocked update becomes approved.
Two review and alert queues clear the update and suppress the stale-source escalation.
Their feeds enter four protocol, risk, and incident summaries.
Eight downstream decisions rely on a fresh-price narrative without a signed update.
